I am 70 years old, and I have grown cotton on this land in Quzhou for most of my life. My father grew it, and I have grown it. Three mu is not much, but it is mine, and I know every corner of it. Some of my children work in the city now, so the heavy work falls mostly to me and whoever is home. I will not change crops at my age — I know cotton, and cotton knows this land.

For seeds, I will go to the village supply shop and buy the same hybrid Bt cotton I have used for the past fifteen or so years. It costs more than old seed but I do not have to spray as much for bollworm, and at 70 my back notices the difference. I will plant in late April after the soil warms.

Before planting I will rotary-till the field — I stopped ploughing deep a few years ago, the rotary tiller is faster and good enough. I will put down base fertilizer at that time: compound fertilizer plus some urea. I will topdress again at the squaring and flowering stages. I have been feeding this land the same way for decades and the yields are steady.

I have the well, so I will irrigate before planting to bring up bottom moisture, then again at squaring, flowering, and boll swelling — four times should do it unless the summer is especially dry.

Even with Bt seed I still get aphids and red spider mites in July and August. I will spray five or six times through the season. That is what the crop needs here.

I expect around 280 jin of seed cotton per mu — that has been my average on this field in recent years.
